title: In vitro comparison of the osteogenic capability of human pulp stem cells on alloplastic, allogeneic, and xenogeneic bone scaffolds
authors: Heitzer M, Modabber A, Zhang X, Winnand P, Zhao Q, Bläsius FM, Buhl EM, Wolf M, Neuss S, Hölzle F, Hildebrand F, Greven J. BMC Oral Health. 2023 Jan 31;23(1):56. doi: 10.1186/s12903-023-02726-4.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “DBBP scaffold led to extremely high cell viability, but also promoted proliferation, attachment, and enhanced the osteogenic differentiation capacity of DPSCs, which hold great potential for bone regeneration treatment ; however, further studies are necessary” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
